#407. Can GTA 6 teach men to be better boyfriends? We asked a relationship therapist.

Since Rockstar released previews of Grand Theft Auto VI this summer, social media has buzzed about the relationship system at the heart of the game. While some critics jumped to say that playing GTA 6 is cheating on your significant other, others speculated that playing the game might actually make players better at IRL connections — especially considering that young adults have less experience.

Now that GTA 6 is out, discussion of the latter has resurfaced on X:

But can making small gestures of affection in a video game actually teach players anything about being a better partner IRL? To answer that question, I reached out to sex and couples therapist Ilana Grines, whom I previously spoke to about whether playing the game is cheating.

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups

Pure — best for anonymous hookups

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity

"We have to be really careful about what we're claiming that video games can actually do for us," Grines said. It's useful when individuals are exposed to behaviors that are typically associated with relationship satisfaction as a whole — like spending time together — but, she said, "your girlfriend doesn't have a meter on her forehead that increased the more you...show her attention."

Part of the online conversation stems from the relationship between GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia, whose connection develops through the player's actions. While players can choose to keep their relationship platonic, the game still tracks their bond. Holding hands, buying flowers, giving compliments, sending texts, and running errands together (which may or may not involve committing crimes) can all improve their relationship score.

The relationship meter gives players a sense of where Jason and Lucia stand with one another, Mashable's editorial director Eric Miller explained to me, a self-professed non-gamer. While previous GTA games have featured romantic relationships and family dynamics, GTA 6 takes things a step further by allowing players to actively shape the protagonists' relationship. Depending on their actions, Jason and Lucia can be running on empty (1/4), partners in crime (2/4), crazy in love (3/4), or hot together (4/4).

Grines is skeptical that simply performing these actions in a game can teach emotional intelligence. "You're literally playing a game when you could be participating in your relationship," Grines continued. That's another line of thinking that's echoed on social media today: That people (mostly men) are doing chores for Lucia instead of their IRL girlfriend.

One of Grines' clients told her that his girlfriend isn't letting him buy the game — but not because of Lucia. It's actually because of the strip club scenes and how realistic the characters look. The girlfriend isn't comfortable with him going to strip clubs in real life, so why would she be comfortable with him going to one in a video game? As in our discussion over whether playing GTA 6 is cheating, Grines said she's entitled to set a boundary.

Real relationships, of course, are more complicated than any in-game relationship meter can capture. And Grines warns against having unrealistic expectations for how video games can improve romance. While seeing a healthy relationship modeled in front of you can be useful, she said that modeling doesn't always create behavioral change. Being a good boyfriend in the game doesn't factor in a real partner's own preferences, emotions, and agency. (For example, your real girlfriend may hate flowers!)

That doesn't mean GTA 6 can't bring couples closer together. Gaming can be a shared experience, as PCMag's Jordan Minor demonstrated when he played the game with his wife.

"It's great that people can experiment and they can repeat actions that may improve their relationship satisfaction," she said. "The real test will be if they can take it out of the video game and into their real lives."

Not everyone likes this element of the game. Right-wing (or right-wing adjacent) influencers Asmongold and Clavicular (who was indicted on two rape charges yesterday) expressed their distaste for GTA 6. The former called the game a "cuck simulator" while playing it on stream, and Clavicular said the game is "insanely cucked."

Then again, GTA 6 is the highest-rated game of all time, so the haters are in the minority.

Anna Iovine is the associate editor of features at Mashable. Previously, as the sex and relationships reporter, she covered topics ranging from dating apps to pelvic pain. #406. Walmart hikes outlook as CEO tells CNBC retailer aims to keep prices low despite soaring fuel costs

Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season.

Walmart said global e-commerce sales surged 17% in the fiscal third quarter, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter.

Walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices.

CEO John Furner told CNBC's Becky Quick that the company has seen higher-than-expected diesel costs, but that tariff refunds have helped the retailer to offset those inputs and maintain lower prices.

"The reality is that increases in diesel fuel and transportation, they do work their way into cost of goods," Furner said in an exclusive interview. "So we're hoping to see these costs come down as soon as possible, and we'll keep prices as low as we can."

CFO John David Rainey told CNBC that growth in online orders for Walmart and Sam's Club was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and reduced prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter.

"This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses."

Walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to increase between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared with previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey said Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance.

Walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

For the quarter ended Oct. 31, the company reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, a year earlier. Revenue rose 5.2%.

Adjusting for investment gains and losses, tax matters and reorganization charges, Walmart earned 65 cents per share.

Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from a year earlier. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount.

Furner also said Walmart is seeing encouraging adoption of its artificial intelligence agent, named Sparky, especially ahead of the holiday season. He said it's led to customer basket increases of 40% on average.

"It just is a great way of just completing the entire basket and solving entire the solution for people," he said.

Sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise.

In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Walmart+ and Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer stand-alone memberships, as well.

Furner told CNBC the new membership has brought roughly 2 million new people into Sam's Club since its launch in late October. Though the company reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey added that it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more."

The company on Thursday said its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter.

The company is typically well insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef.

Rainey said Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start."

The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership.

Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year to date.

For other protein powder recommendations, check out some of our other tested favorites.

It’s BPA- and phthalate-free, dishwasher-safe, and available in three sizes (20, 28, and 45 ounces).

Creatine won’t turn you into the Rock overnight, but when paired with regular weightlifting and a nutritious diet, it can help preserve strength and lean body mass. (But your gym bro probably already knows this.) There are several versions of creatine out there, but it’s best to stick to monohydrate; it’s the most studied, the most reliable, and usually the most affordable. Thorne’s flavorless powder is perfect for blending into smoothies or mixing with water before a workout.

Pro tip: When they hit you with a “Bro, I’m looking swole lately” after three days on creatine, maybe don’t mention it’s mostly water weight. Let them have this one.

Body scales—like dietary supplements—should be a request, not a surprise; I would only gift one if they’ve explicitly said they want one. Nevertheless, this scale is for the gym rat who tracks macros in their sleep. If they’re logging every rep, meal, and REM cycle, they’ll love the Runstar FG2015 Smart Scale. Unlike a standard foot-only scale, this one has a retractable handle with electrodes that scan your whole body and analyze muscle mass, water weight, and visceral fat. Does the average person need that level of detail? No, but if they’re bodybuilding, bulking, or just like to boast about their body fat percentage down to the decimal, it’s a total game-changer.

For more recommendations, we weighed in on other smart scales in this guide.

The Hydro Flask is the ultimate gift for a gym lover. Built like a dumbbell, it can survive drops, dents, and tosses into any gym bag or back seat. It keeps water cold for hours and comes in a ton of sizes and colors. Order directly from the site to customize the lid, strap, and bottle; you can also engrave their name so no one accidentally walks off with their bottle again.

It folds in half for easy storage and fits a range of rider heights and sizes. It has an upgraded motor from the original, but Quad Squad bros know to turn it off and pedal this 71-pound beast with pure leg strength for a real workout. —Harry Rabinowitz

Some of our favorite gym workout headphones, the BlueAnt Pump X, have a pretty remarkable standout feature. You can swap out the regular ear pads for cooling gel ear pads, which you can store in the fridge when you’re not using them. If your bro has ever found that keeping noise-canceling headphones on his head while he concentrates on his form makes him feel too sweaty, these are worth a shot. They work remarkably well, even if the condiment drawer in the fridge is a weird place to store workout equipment. —Adrienne So

#403. Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment

The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most important temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

The Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

The east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess Athena from the head of her father Zeus, surrounded by the Olympian gods. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3.8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann heads the Antiquities and Asia department at Frankfurt's Liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

The results are now on display in an exhibition at the Liebieghaus titled "Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle."

Only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

In 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the British Museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Then, in 2014, a visit to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!"

Nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in Rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go."

The researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3D scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

Digitally fitting the fragments together led to another important discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

The Romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment." This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Using a 3D printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7.7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most important fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

Alongside works from the Liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the Vatican Museums and the Louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

There is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

In the early 19th century, Elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

For years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

The exhibition "Athena, the Stage is Yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

This article was originally written in German.

#401. Gap stock soars as retailer says Old Navy turnaround shows signs of improvement

Gap Inc. on Thursday announced Ashley Kechter will be the next president and CEO of its Athleta brand, effective Dec. 14.

The retailer also said Old Navy's turnaround is showing signs of progress, sending shares up more than 12% in trading Friday.

Kechter comes to Gap from activewear retailer Vuori, where she was global president and oversaw the brand's global business strategy, marketing and financials. She was previously global brand president of Fabletics and began her career at Gap before that.

"I'm excited to return to Gap Inc. and partner with [Gap CEO Richard Dickson] and the team to strengthen our connection with customers and shape the brand's next chapter," Kechter said in a statement.

The announcement comes after Lululemon poached former Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger to be its chief product officer last month.

"Clearly, we're disappointed with Athleta's performance, and we recognize there's a lot of work ahead," Dickson told CNBC. "We had been in rebuild mode, but now we're really in turnaround mode."

Dickson said the company is focused on getting back to its fundamentals: fabrications, feature, form, function and fit. Dickson added that Kechter will be conducting a "comprehensive review" of the brand to reposition Athleta for future success.

While the execution of its strategy has thus far "fallen short," Dickson said this new approach will allow Athleta to fully realize its potential.

Gap also reported mixed fiscal third-quarter earnings on Thursday and posted flat overall comparable sales. Wall Street had been expecting a comparable sales increase of 1.3%, according to StreetAccount.

Net sales grew 2%, though demand softened in October and early November due to warmer weather, the company said. Store sales increased 1%, while online sales increased 3%.

Gap also said it's recorded a $420 million adjustment to cost of goods sold and a $21 million adjustment to interest income from tariff refunds so far this year.

The company lowered its full-year net sales outlook to be "roughly flat," down from previous guidance of up between 1% and 1.5%. Gap is also now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $2.29 and $2.34, down from an earlier expectation of between $2.35 and $2.45 per share.

Dickson said in an interview that much of the lowered guidance was due to warmer weather in the first two weeks of the quarter, but he said Gap is expecting "meaningful acceleration" in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.

"We're monitoring the trends, and we're going to remain agile as we respond to the changing business trends," Dickson said.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

For the quarter, Gap reported net income of $311 million, or 86 cents per share, compared with $236 million, or 62 cents per share, the year prior. Sales rose slightly from $3.94 billion the year prior.

At Athleta, net sales were down 14% compared with last year, coming in at $220 million. Comparable sales for the banner sank 15%, which the company attributed to "limited traction" from efforts to modernize its merchandise and marketing. `

The company's namesake brand saw 9% comparable sales growth for the quarter, with net sales of $1.1 billion, marking an 11% increase compared with last year. Dickson said it was the brand's 12th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales.

"Gap is really firing on all cylinders, and the consistency of the brand is really giving us confidence in the brand's ability to continue its momentum," Dickson said.

The Old Navy banner saw flat comparable sales for the quarter and net sales of $2.3 billion, up 1% compared with last year. It's the first earnings report since the brand, which has been experiencing sluggish sales, named Michael Francis as its new CEO last quarter. Francis began his role at Old Navy on Nov. 2.

Banana Republic saw its net sales sink 3% compared with last year, which the company attributed to delayed demand for cold-weather categories and a women's fall assortment that fell flat. Wall Street had been expecting growth of 1.5%, according to StreetAccount.

Dickson said the brand has since introduced new products and seen demand "rebound" as cooler weather has set in across the country.

"We've been encouraged by the early customer response, and we should see sequential improvement in the fourth quarter," he said. "There's some work to do here, but with peak selling still ahead, I'm confident that the team is focused on the right areas and [will] ultimately position Banana well for growth."

#400. ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Is a Perfect Game. Rushing Through It Would Be a Mistake

Hey, maybe don’t just immediately go to the strip club. Look, I know that’s what you want to do right away when you start Grand Theft Auto VI. This is a GTA game after all—that sort of outlet for titillation is a common theme in this franchise. But going straight to the good stuff isn’t the best way to play this game.

The biggest video game ever has turned out to be one of the very best. With near-universally perfect review scores, GTA VI has emerged as an absolute behemoth that has lived up to 13 years of hype.

I’ve spent a few hours in the game, and one thing becomes clear right away: This game is a slow burn. The GTA franchise has always been high-octane, arcade-style, prioritizing hyperviolence and exaggerated physics that let your character go wild in the digital sandbox. But the latest installation is much more reserved. Vehicles and player movements feel heavier. The characters have deeper, more emotional backstories and motivations. The world has more interactivity and reacts to your actions in much more varied ways.

It evokes a play style that feels very much in common with Rockstar’s previous title, Red Dead Redemption 2. It was a Western that made the player feel the friction of an often slow, plodding life that didn’t shy away from simulating all the chores of a horse-bound cowboy in the 1800s. GTA VI, set in the modern era, is faster-paced but still carries that intentionality to slow the player down.

That manifests in ways that might feel like busywork. Instead of having access to all your weapons and outfits, you have to make space for the things you want to bring with you and store everything else in the back of your car. You have to call someone to fix your car and wait for them to arrive. Yeah, you have to paint your house and buy your girlfriend flowers. Get used to it. This can sometimes feel like a chore, but it slows the player down to give them time to examine the world around them.

Once you start looking around and really take everything in, the level of detail is truly unique. Leonida—GTA VI’s mirror version of Miami, Florida—is so varied and splendid it is almost overwhelming. After the game’s on-the-rails introductory missions open up into the first opportunity for an open-world sojourn, the sheer scale of this world becomes apparent. Zooming out on the map and seeing the vast expanse of unexplored territory is dizzying.

There is just so much Leonida, and none of it feels sparse or unfinished. Every place, person, animal, and environmental asset feels fully fleshed out. Driving down the road, with other cars zooming past, is photorealistic enough to look nearly like real dash-cam footage. This game, as I have muttered to myself over and over again while playing, “is simply insane.”

If you’ve followed the GTA VI saga, this likely won’t surprise you. Developer Rockstar and its parent company Take-Two have spent around a billion dollars to develop the game. It’s taken 13 years. The company even delayed the game multiple times to make sure it was polished.

There is massive hype, and at this point I’d say what Rockstar has achieved here has surpassed that hype. The game is likely to be the pinnacle of this era of video games, the final grand blockbuster achieved without the use of generative AI.

I’ve been playing GTA games for a long time. I’ll probably be playing this one for the rest of my life. Like me, you’re probably very excited to dive into this gigantic world. The best way to do that is not to try to see it all at once. Pace yourself. Look out for the small moments, as they may lead to something more profound than you’re expecting. Slow down, and you can really feel how the world reacts.

Nothing else like this game exists. And there probably won’t be for a very long time. Might as well make it last.

#399. 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine

The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

Once again, Berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on Ukraine: Around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across Europe, are set to gather in the German capital on Thursday (November 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Extensive security measures have already been announced for Berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

The "Coalition of the Willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Led by Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within Ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London.

But what can the coalition realistically achieve? Stefan Meister of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) is not overly optimistic.

"The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal," he told DW. "There is no plan outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises."

Nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

This has sparked a debate among EU heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent Europe in such talks. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)?

After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, Merz said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear."

But what exactly did that mean? That Germany alone would speak for all of Europe? Hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President Antonio Costa, would also take part.

Stefan Meister of the DGAP believes the debate says a great deal about the pressures Europe itself is under.

"Europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations," Meister said. "Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that."

German Deputy Government Spokesperson Sebastian Hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on Monday over a possible role for Friedrich Merz as chief negotiator.

At the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

US negotiator Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, struck a rather different tone last week.

Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he said: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations."

Government spokesperson Hille responded on Monday: "Europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question."

Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: Peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

European supporters of Ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in Germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

According to the latest DeutschlandTrend survey on the issue, conducted or German public broadcaster ARD in September 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to Ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

A further study conducted for public broadcaster WDR in November 2026 found that support for Ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in Germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

This article was originally written in German.
